## Data


```{r data}
rent <- c(12500, 13800, 11200, 15000, 12500, 26000,
          14300, 13100, 12500, 16700, 14900, 13600)
```

## Q1
```{r}
mean(rent)
median(rent)
table(rent)
```
## Q2

One apartment rents for NT$26,000, which is far above the rest.

```{r}
rent2 <- rent[rent != 26000]

mean(rent2)
median(rent2)
```
## Q3

The mean changes more than the median.

The median better describes the typical rent near campus because it is less affected by the unusually high rent of NT$26,000.
